correctness.rationale: A disconnected induced subset with an isolated vertex is contained in its row–column cross and yields precisely the row, column or two-arm form; otherwise, one edge in one component forces the other component to use the two cross-corners, and no isolates force exactly a 2-by-2 rectangle. Case separation is unique. Inclusion-maximal disconnected subsets are full crosses and rectangles, yielding cut counts and sizes. Direct independent brute-force BFS checked 1,151,488 labeled subsets across (3,3),(3,4),(3,5),(4,4),(4,5), including coefficients and inclusion-maximality. Reliability treats empty survivor separately and follows by summing Bernoulli weights. Finite tests do not replace the unrestricted proof.

value.rationale: The polynomial enumerates every vertex-failure pattern leading to disconnected operation and determines nonempty-connected network reliability. Its maximal-disconnected-set duality completely classifies all inclusion-minimal cuts in a natural infinite symmetric graph family, including a structurally different second family with unbounded cut-size gap. These are meaningful structural and probabilistic invariants beyond preexisting scalar minimum connectivity; not an arbitrary single coefficient.
